entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
-
This writ petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, seeking the following relief:
"...to pass an order or orders or direction more particularly one in the nature of a writ of mandamus declaring that the action of Respondent No's. 2 to 5 herein in not considering the representation dated 12.07.2023 with regard to deviations of the Kovvada canal by acquiring petitioner's private land which is passing through petitioner agricultural land to an extent of Ac.5.90 cents in Rs.No. 225/2C and 225/2D situated at Kovvurupadu village, Gopalapuram Mandal, as wholly illegal,
arbitrary, unjust, untenable, unconstitutional, Contrary to principles of natural justice, besides being violative of Petitioner's rights guaranteed under Article 14, 21 and 300-A of Constitution of India wholly illegal, arbitrary, unjust, untenable,
unconstitutional, Contrary to principles of natural justice, besides being violative of Petitioner's rights guaranteed under Article 14, 21 and 300-A of Constitution of India and consequently direct the 2to 5 Respondents herein to consider the representation given by the petitioner dated 12.07.2023 and pass such further order or other orders..."
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the respondents.
3. The petitioner is the absolute owner and possessor of the land admeasuring Ac.5.90 cents in Rs.No.225/2C and 225/2D situated at Kovvurupadu village, Gopalapuram Mandal.
The subject land was acquired from his vendor through a registered sale deed dated 06.06.2014 and 13.05.2023.
Since then, he has been in possession and enjoyment of the said property.

It is further the case of the petitioner that before the acquisition of the land by the petitioner from his vendor, the respondent authorities initiated the land acquisition proceedings and acquired an extent of Ac.0.66 cents from the petitioner's vendor in Sy.No.225/2 in the year 2004 for formation of a minor irrigation canal.
After acquisition of the said land, the respondent authorities laid/formed the minor irrigation canal through the land owned by the vendor of the petitioner.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that after the acquisition of the remaining land by the petitioner from his vendor, it seems that because of deviation in formation of minor irrigation canal,
the respondent authorities occupied more of the land than they actually acquired.

For which, the petitioner as well as his vendor submitted representations time and again for conducting a due survey and for demarcation of the subject land to determine whether any excess land of the petitioner was under the occupation of the minor irrigation canal.
Finally, the petitioner submitted his representation on 12.07.2023.
Even after such representation, the respondents neither considered the same nor passed any order to conduct the survey and demarcation of the subject land as requested by the petitioner.
Hence, the writ petition.

On the other hand, the learned Government Pleader for Irrigation furnishes written instructions by respondent No.4 dated 20.12.2023, wherein it is stated that the Kovvadu Caulva Reservoir is a medium irrigation reservoir and has left and right main canals.
The petitioners land bearing Survey No.225/2 is existing in the 5L minor of IR Distributaries.
The compensation was paid in the year 2004 to Survey No.225/2 for an extent of Ac.0.66 cents for the excavation/formation of the above minor canal, and the said excavation was done in the year 2005.

During the execution of work, the then officers changed the original canal alignment with the consent of the then land owner for smooth running of water to the ayacutdars and as per the site conditions.

During the excavation, Sri P.Gowtham Varma, S/o Venkata Narasimha Raju, was the actual owner of the above land, and with the consent of the land owner and local farmers, the changes were made by the then respondent officers.

7. Learned Government Pleader for Irrigation further submits that after the acquisition of the subject land, i.e., A.c.0.66 cents in Sy.No.225/2 of Kovvurupadu village, from the vendor of the petitioner herein in the year 2004, the minor irrigation canal through the subject land was laid.
While laying the subject canal, there is a deviation from the original plan for the purpose of free flow of water to cater to the needs of the ryots/ayacutdars.

He further submits NV, J W.P. No. 32750 OF 2023 that, pursuant to the request of the petitioner on 04.09.2017, the 3rd respondent herein submitted a report dated 09.10.2017, wherein he admitted the deviation from the original plan.
The said deviation was made in the year 2005 itself.
The petitioner acquired the land only in the year 2013-2014, i.e., after the deviation of the subject canal.
Hence, the claim of the petitioner is liable to be dismissed since the deviation was already in existence before the acquisition of the land by the petitioner.

In respect of the other claim of the petitioner to conduct a survey and demarcation of the subject land to identify the deviation, but the respondent authorities have neither conducted any survey nor demarcated it.
Therefore, this Court can direct the respondent authorities to conduct the survey and demarcation of the subject land.

8. Having regard to the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Government Pleader for Irrigation, and on perusal of material available on record, without going into the merits of the case, the present Writ Petition is disposed of directing the respondent Nos.3 and 5 herein to conduct the survey and demarcation by following the due procedure as contemplated under the provisions of the Survey and Boundaries Act, 1923, by providing an Basava Naga Lakshmmi vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184228670/
2 opportunity to the petitioner and other stake holders if any.

sentences.text: After such survey and demarcation, if the respondents found that the land occupied by the subject minor irrigation canal is only Ac.0.66 cents, NV, J W.P. No. 32750 OF 2023 the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation since his vendor has already received the Award Amount.

If such occupation is more than Ac.0.66 cents, the petitioner is entitled for compensation, and accordingly, the respondents shall pay the compensation to the petitioner by following due procedure as contemplated under the law.

The entire exercise of the survey and demarcation should be completed within a period of three (03)
months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

9. It is further observed that the petitioner, being an agriculturist, and his land is adjacent to the subject minor irrigation canal, he is entitled to draw the water for irrigation of his agricultural field.
Therefore, respondents are restrained from interfering with the petitioner's drawing of water from the minor irrigation canal for agricultural purposes.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Consequently, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in the writ petition shall stand closed.

VENKATESWARLU NIMMAGADDA, J Date:
